questions.objective: Explain the purpose and scope of MCP and the integration problem it standardizes between AI applications and external systems
questions.prompt: Without a shared protocol, an organization connecting N AI applications to M external systems must build and maintain roughly how many custom integrations?
options: M minus N separate integrations
N multiplied by M separate integrations
A single integration shared by every application
N plus M separate integrations
questions.explanation: Each application-system pair needs its own custom connector without a shared protocol, so the integration count grows as N times M. A standard protocol like MCP turns that multiplicative cost into an additive N plus M relationship.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原B(1)N×M是逐pair自定义接口计数的理想假设，MCP N+M是接口成本模型非任意SDK/权限均互通保证。
source_correct_options: N multiplied by M separate integrations

questions.objective: Describe the core MCP concepts of hosts, clients, servers, primitives, and the stateless JSON-RPC request model
questions.prompt: In MCP 2026-07-28, what may a server use to decide how to answer a new request?
options: The sequence of earlier calls made on the same connection
Assumptions carried over from the previous request it answered
The fields inside that request, plus any handle it names
A session object created when the connection was first opened
questions.explanation: MCP 2026-07-28 is stateless: a server must treat each request as self-describing and must not infer identity, version, or capabilities from earlier traffic on the same connection. Any state that spans calls travels explicitly as a server-minted handle passed back as an argument.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原C(2)每请求explicit fields+handle；业务store与ACL/currentpolicy另核，handle本身不授权。
source_correct_options: The fields inside that request, plus any handle it names

questions.objective: Reason about interoperability, protocol versioning, and the value of one open protocol over per-system custom integrations
questions.prompt: A client sends a request and receives UnsupportedProtocolVersionError. What should it do next?
options: Resend the identical unchanged request and simply wait for a new result
Fall back permanently to the older 2024-11-05 initialize handshake flow
Close the connection permanently and refuse to contact that server again
Retry the request once using a version from the error's supported list
questions.explanation: UnsupportedProtocolVersionError carries the versions the server supports in its data, so a client negotiates by retrying with one of those values rather than guessing, giving up, or assuming a legacy handshake is required.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原D(3)在client/server共同支持版本中重试−32022，不盲server[0]；once只是此scenario预算，不普遍只准一次。
source_correct_options: Retry the request once using a version from the error's supported list

questions.objective: Read the MCP specification, its revision history, and its feature lifecycle to tell current, deprecated, and removed behavior apart
questions.prompt: In the MCP specification's use of RFC 2119 keywords, what does a requirement written with MUST mean for an implementation?
options: The behavior is mandatory, and non-conformant implementations fail
The behavior is recommended but implementations may reasonably skip it
The behavior is one optional idea among several equally valid designs
The behavior is only a suggestion for future specification drafts
questions.explanation: RFC 2119 and RFC 8174 define MUST as an absolute requirement. Reading requirement strength correctly separates mandatory behavior from SHOULD recommendations and MAY options, which is essential for interpreting any specification clause precisely.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原A(0)规范MUST在适用条件为要求；MUST是否落实需实现证据，非规范文字自动测试失败。
source_correct_options: The behavior is mandatory, and non-conformant implementations fail

questions.objective: Describe the core MCP concepts of hosts, clients, servers, primitives, and the stateless JSON-RPC request model
questions.prompt: Which two statements correctly describe MCP's JSON-RPC message shapes? Select two.
options: Several requests may still be batched together inside one array
A request's id must be non-null and cannot repeat a still-pending id
A result response may safely omit resultType whenever a server prefers
A notification never carries an id and never gets a reply
questions.explanation: A notification has no id and the receiver must never answer it, while a request id must be non-null and must not repeat while an earlier request with that id is still awaiting a response. Batching was removed, and a modern result must include resultType.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原B/D(1,3)notification noid/noresponse，request非null不重复pending；legacymissingresultType按complete兼容，现代必须明确。
source_correct_options: A request's id must be non-null and cannot repeat a still-pending id
A notification never carries an id and never gets a reply

questions.objective: Read the schemas and structured data that define MCP messages, tool definitions, capabilities, and server manifests
questions.prompt: A tool definition omits its annotations object entirely. Under the default values, how should a client treat that tool?
options: As destructive, read-only, idempotent, and closed-world
As destructive, not read-only, not idempotent, and open-world
As non-destructive, non-idempotent, closed-world, and read-only
As read-only, non-destructive, idempotent, and closed-world
questions.explanation: When annotations are omitted, the defaults apply: readOnlyHint false, destructiveHint true, idempotentHint false, and openWorldHint true. Clients must treat these as untrusted hints from the server, not enforced guarantees, when deciding whether to prompt for confirmation.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原B(1)default readonlyfalse/destructivetrue/idempotentfalse/openworldtrue都是不可信提示，不是实现安全保证。
source_correct_options: As destructive, not read-only, not idempotent, and open-world

questions.objective: Read the schemas and structured data that define MCP messages, tool definitions, capabilities, and server manifests
questions.prompt: A server publishes a tool that takes no parameters. Which inputSchema value is correct for that tool under 2026-07-28?
options: An empty JSON array standing in for the schema
A null value marking the tool as taking no arguments
An object schema with type object and additionalProperties false
Leaving inputSchema absent from the tool definition entirely
questions.explanation: inputSchema is never null and is never left out; a tool that takes no parameters still declares an object schema, conventionally type object with additionalProperties false, so only an empty arguments object validates against it.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原C(2)空参数object/additionalPropertiesfalse，schema不能null/缺省；其它JSON schema完整验证另核。
source_correct_options: An object schema with type object and additionalProperties false

questions.objective: Distinguish the responsibilities of MCP hosts, clients, and servers and how discovery and capability negotiation connect them
questions.prompt: Which two statements correctly describe how a host manages connections to multiple MCP servers? Select two.
options: Colliding tool names from different servers are disambiguated with a server prefix
A server's self-reported serverInfo.name is guaranteed unique for routing
One client instance is shared across every server connection
The host embeds a separate client for each server connection
questions.explanation: A host binds one client to each server so responsibilities and trust stay separated, and it commonly prefixes tool names by server identifier to resolve collisions, since serverInfo is self-reported and not guaranteed unique.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原A/D(0,3)oneclientperserver/稳定qualifiedmapping，prefix建议与alias碰撞核，不信自报serverInfo唯一。
source_correct_options: Colliding tool names from different servers are disambiguated with a server prefix
The host embeds a separate client for each server connection

questions.objective: Trace the model interaction flow from a user request through the host, model, client, and server and back into model context
questions.prompt: A tool call returns a result with isError true because the arguments failed validation. What should the host do with that result?
options: Silently drop the call without ever informing the model
Treat it exactly like a protocol error and stop all retries
Discard the conversation and restart the request from scratch
Feed the error content back so the model can retry correctly
questions.explanation: Tool execution errors are ordinary results carrying isError and explanatory content, designed to flow back into the model's context so the model can revise its arguments and try again, unlike a protocol-level failure.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原D(3)knownschema failure toolerror可回model修复；retry需预算/currentpermission，不所有isError自动重试。
source_correct_options: Feed the error content back so the model can retry correctly

questions.objective: Apply the request, notification, subscription, and multi round-trip interaction patterns and handle each result type
questions.prompt: A client answers an input_required result from a tools/call request. How should it send its answers back to the server?
options: Retry the same request with a new id and matching requestState
Open a brand-new elicitation/create request completely on its own
Reply by reusing the original request id the server first saw
Send it as a notification, since no server reply is expected
questions.explanation: Multi round-trip requests require the retry to carry a new JSON-RPC id along with inputResponses and the requestState echoed exactly as received; reusing the old id or inventing a fresh state value breaks the round trip.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原A(0)新id/inputResponses/已有state精确echo；若源未给state禁止自行加，选项matchingstate需此条件。
source_correct_options: Retry the same request with a new id and matching requestState

questions.objective: Apply the request, notification, subscription, and multi round-trip interaction patterns and handle each result type
questions.prompt: What must be the first message a server sends after accepting a subscriptions/listen request?
options: A progress notification carrying the newly assigned subscriptionId
An acknowledged message naming the filters the server will honor
The first list_changed notification that happens to be pending
An empty result that closes the stream right after it opens
questions.explanation: The stream must open with an acknowledgment naming the subset of requested notification types the server will actually honor, before any list-changed or resource-updated events, so the client knows exactly what it will receive.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原B(1)firstack只所请求filters允许子集，exactsubscriptionId与stream lifecycle必须。
source_correct_options: An acknowledged message naming the filters the server will honor

questions.objective: Apply the request, notification, subscription, and multi round-trip interaction patterns and handle each result type
questions.prompt: Which two statements are true about the tasks extension in 2026-07-28? Select two.
options: A client polls task progress by repeatedly calling tasks/list
tasks/cancel asks the server to stop cooperatively, not instantly
A client must declare the extension before a server returns a task
Tasks belong to the required core protocol every server implements
questions.explanation: Tasks moved out of the core protocol into an opt-in extension, so a server only returns a task result when the client has declared support, the client polls with tasks/get rather than a list method, and cancellation is cooperative rather than instant.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原B/C(1,2)双方协商Tasks，getpoll/cancelcooperative；taskhandle需owner/durable，cancelack不证effectrollback。
source_correct_options: tasks/cancel asks the server to stop cooperatively, not instantly
A client must declare the extension before a server returns a task

questions.objective: Handle protocol errors and tool execution errors, including version, capability, header, and validation failures
questions.prompt: An unknown tool name, an invalid prompt name, and a missing required prompt argument all map to which JSON-RPC error code in 2026-07-28?
options: -32021, because the client is missing a required capability
-32601, because each names a method the server does not recognize
-32602, because each is an invalid-parameters failure before any execution
-32002, the legacy not-found code every current server should still emit
questions.explanation: All three failures are recognized before any tool or prompt runs, so 2026-07-28 groups them under Invalid params rather than treating them as unknown methods, legacy not-found errors, or a missing client capability.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原C(2)unknowntool、badpromptname、missingpromptarg为−32602；recognizedmethod与knowntool inputSchema错误通道不同。
source_correct_options: -32602, because each is an invalid-parameters failure before any execution

questions.objective: Handle protocol errors and tool execution errors, including version, capability, header, and validation failures
questions.prompt: An HTTP request's Mcp-Method header names tools/call, but the JSON body's method field says prompts/get. What should the server do?
options: Merge both methods and attempt to satisfy each partially
Process the request as tools/call because headers take precedence
Trust the JSON body and silently ignore the header value
Reject it with -32020 because the header disagrees with the body
questions.explanation: Required headers exist so gateways can route without parsing bodies, so a server must reject a request whose header disagrees with its body using the HeaderMismatch code rather than picking one side or blending both methods.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原D(3)mirror mismatch−32020在effect前，requiredheader存在/大小写/重复+bodyvalidation独立。
source_correct_options: Reject it with -32020 because the header disagrees with the body

questions.objective: Walk the tool invocation lifecycle from discovery and selection through call, user input, progress, cancellation, and result
questions.prompt: A tool call's Streamable HTTP response stream breaks before a result arrives. What is the correct recovery?
options: Reissue the same call as a new request with a new id
Treat the broken stream as a successful empty result
Abandon the tool entirely and remove it from the tool list
Wait indefinitely on the same stream since the result is still coming
questions.explanation: A broken stream loses whatever response was in flight, and since MCP dropped stream resumability, the only correct recovery is reissuing the call as a fresh request with a new id rather than waiting forever or assuming success.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原A(0)为唯一近意选项，但'onlycorrect reissue anycall'危险过强；副作用effect可能已commit，先receipt/reconcile/业务幂等再决定重试，断流不等失败/rollback。
source_correct_options: Reissue the same call as a new request with a new id

questions.objective: Identify the protocol primitives and utilities, including tools, resources, prompts, completion, caching, pagination, transports, and deprecated client features
questions.prompt: Which two features are deprecated but still functional in MCP 2026-07-28? Select two.
options: Roots, reached now through a multi round-trip input request
Sampling, reached now through a multi round-trip input request
The subscriptions/listen request used to open a notification stream
The server/discover request every server must implement
questions.explanation: Roots and sampling were deprecated in 2026-07-28 but keep working through multi round-trip input requests of type roots/list and sampling/createMessage, unlike server/discover and subscriptions/listen, which remain current, non-deprecated parts of the core protocol.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原A/B(0,1)Roots/Sampling deprecated仍MRTR，最早移除不等已经移除，clientmode能力每请求核。
source_correct_options: Roots, reached now through a multi round-trip input request
Sampling, reached now through a multi round-trip input request

questions.objective: Identify the protocol primitives and utilities, including tools, resources, prompts, completion, caching, pagination, transports, and deprecated client features
questions.prompt: A resources/read result is marked cacheScope public. What does that scope actually control?
options: Whether the server enforces access control before returning the resource
Whether the cached entry may be shared across different users and tokens
Whether the resource content itself is readable by any user
Whether the underlying file on disk is writable by the client
questions.explanation: cacheScope only governs whether a cached response may be reused across different callers; it is never an access-control mechanism, so a server must still authorize every read independent of whether the result happens to be publicly cacheable.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原B(1)publiccache可分享但不替ACL/currentpermission/TTL，私密context不误设public。
source_correct_options: Whether the cached entry may be shared across different users and tokens

questions.objective: Locate the trust boundaries between host, client, server, model, and the tools and content a server exposes
questions.prompt: A server's discover result reports serverInfo with a trustworthy-sounding name. What role may serverInfo correctly play?
options: Proof that the server's tool descriptions are safe to trust
Granting that server elevated access without further checks
Display and logging only, never an authorization decision
A substitute for validating the server's OAuth token audience
questions.explanation: clientInfo and serverInfo are self-reported fields meant for display, logging, and debugging. A host must never use them to grant access, vouch for tool safety, or replace audience validation, since any server can claim any name.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原C(2)自报serverInfo仅display/log/debug，hash/名称不替authaud/provenance。
source_correct_options: Display and logging only, never an authorization decision

questions.objective: Apply OAuth-based authorization, client registration, scopes, and user consent so a user approves what a server may see and do
questions.prompt: An authorization server's metadata does not list code_challenge_methods_supported. What must a compliant MCP client do?
options: Fall back to sending the client secret in the URL
Assume S256 support and continue the flow as normal
Proceed without PKCE since the field is optional for legacy servers
Refuse to proceed with authorization against that server
questions.explanation: PKCE is mandatory for every MCP authorization flow, so when an authorization server does not advertise its supported challenge methods the client cannot confirm PKCE support and must refuse to continue rather than guessing or skipping it.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原D(3)该HTTP交互授权profile不能确认PKCE时拒；sourceeveryauthorizationflow措辞过强，CC机器grant不是PKCEcodeflow。
source_correct_options: Refuse to proceed with authorization against that server

questions.objective: Apply OAuth-based authorization, client registration, scopes, and user consent so a user approves what a server may see and do
questions.prompt: An MCP client has no pre-registered credentials, and the authorization server advertises client_id_metadata_document_supported. What should it try next?
options: Register using a Client ID Metadata Document at an HTTPS URL
Wait for the server to push credentials to the client
Skip straight to Dynamic Client Registration since it is fastest
Ask the end user to type in a client id manually
questions.explanation: The registration priority places pre-registration first, then Client ID Metadata Documents whenever the authorization server advertises support for them, ahead of the deprecated Dynamic Client Registration path and asking the user as a last resort.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原A(0)本issuer未pre-reg且advertisedCIMD，exactURL/docredirect安全fetch/政策独立，不自动任意AS接受。
source_correct_options: Register using a Client ID Metadata Document at an HTTPS URL

questions.objective: Apply OAuth-based authorization, client registration, scopes, and user consent so a user approves what a server may see and do
questions.prompt: A request fails with 403 and error insufficient_scope, listing three required scopes the client never held. What should the client request on retry?
options: The same original scope set, unchanged, retried again until it works
The union of its earlier granted scopes and the newly required ones
Every scope the authorization server has ever defined, just to be safe
Only the three newly required scopes, dropping what it already held
questions.explanation: Step-up authorization asks for the union of the client's prior scopes and the scopes named in the challenge, within a limited number of retries, so access grows precisely rather than shrinking, over-requesting, or repeating an insufficient request unchanged.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原B(1)prior+requiredunion且bounded新AS授权，不本地集合等token权限。
source_correct_options: The union of its earlier granted scopes and the newly required ones

questions.objective: Choose risk and safety controls against tool poisoning, injection, token misuse, and over-broad access
questions.prompt: Which two practices help a host defend against a tool definition changing maliciously after a user first approved it? Select two.
options: Trusting every list_changed notification as automatically re-approved
Disabling tools/list caching entirely so nothing is ever pinned
Treating a changed listing as a rug pull until it is re-reviewed
Pinning approved tool definitions and reviewing any change before reuse
questions.explanation: A rug pull happens when a previously approved tool's definition drifts silently, so defenses pin the approved definition and hold any change for re-review rather than auto-trusting every update or abandoning caching altogether, which would not by itself detect drift.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原C/D(2,3)whole-descriptor/artifactpolicy pin与当前driftre-review，哈希稳定不是无恶意，目录通知不自动批准。
source_correct_options: Treating a changed listing as a rug pull until it is re-reviewed
Pinning approved tool definitions and reviewing any change before reuse

questions.objective: Design auditability and observability so protocol activity can be traced, attributed, and reviewed
questions.prompt: A request carries traceparent in its _meta and calls through to an upstream system. What should happen to that trace context?
options: It is stored only in server logs and never forwarded onward
It is regenerated at every hop so each hop gets a new trace
It propagates through the call chain so spans share one trace id
It is discarded once the request leaves the originating client
questions.explanation: W3C Trace Context fields such as traceparent are meant to propagate across the whole call chain so that spans in the host, client, server, and any upstream system can be correlated under one shared trace id for observability.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原C(2)保trace新span，与sampledbit/parent/敏感baggage/跨信任传播控制独立；caller自选trace不证真实关联。
source_correct_options: It propagates through the call chain so spans share one trace id

questions.objective: Design auditability and observability so protocol activity can be traced, attributed, and reviewed
questions.prompt: An audit log needs to prove that no earlier record was altered after the fact. What technique gives that tamper evidence?
options: Encrypting the log so only an administrator can open the file
Rotating the log file each day and deleting the old copies
Storing every record in a plain text file with no structure
Chaining each record's checksum to the one stored before it
questions.explanation: A hash chain links each audit record to the hash of its predecessor, so altering or removing any earlier entry breaks the chain and is detectable, which plain storage, rotation, or encryption alone do not guarantee.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原D(3)只本地chain一致性，整链重算/删除尾部可过；需独立可信head/appendstorage/签名才能较强tamper evidence，原任意edit/removal必detect不成立。
source_correct_options: Chaining each record's checksum to the one stored before it

questions.objective: Map the roles, responsibilities, governance, and adoption patterns of teams building and deploying MCP
questions.prompt: A proposed change to the MCP specification has been merged as a Final SEP, and its deprecation window has now elapsed. Who decides to actually remove that feature?
options: The Core Maintainers, after the minimum deprecation window has passed
An automated script once the deprecation window elapses
Any single contributor who opens a pull request
The end users of the AI application, by majority vote
questions.explanation: The feature lifecycle sets a minimum deprecation window, but reaching that window only makes removal eligible; the Core Maintainers still decide when a deprecated feature is actually removed, rather than an individual contributor, a vote, or automation.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原A(0)minimum资格到期仍由maintainers决定，不自动删除；已selecteddeprecated条件支持，具体治理当前行政全页未新核。
source_correct_options: The Core Maintainers, after the minimum deprecation window has passed

questions.objective: Map the roles, responsibilities, governance, and adoption patterns of teams building and deploying MCP
questions.prompt: A team deploys an MCP server that runs as a local stdio subprocess. Whose responsibility is it to supply that server's credentials?
options: The model, which requests them through a tool call
The operator, who provides them through the local environment
The end user, typed into the model's chat window
The authorization server, through a browser redirect flow
questions.explanation: stdio servers should not run the OAuth browser flow and instead read credentials from the environment the operator controls, which is a deployment responsibility distinct from asking the end user directly or routing credentials through the model or a redirect.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原B(1)stdio凭证通常受控环境/config注入，非用户chat/model秘密，环境存在不替credentialaud/最小权限。
source_correct_options: The operator, who provides them through the local environment

questions.objective: Select operational use cases and the primitives or extensions that fit each one
questions.prompt: Which three recommendations correctly match a use case to its fitting MCP mechanism? Select three.
options: A read of one user's private data should cache with a private cacheScope
A user-initiated slash-command template should be exposed as a tool
A multi-minute build job should use the tasks extension
A machine-to-machine integration with no human present should use the client credentials extension

A multi-minute build job should use the tasks extension
A machine-to-machine integration with no human present should use the client credentials extension

questions.objective: Select operational use cases and the primitives or extensions that fit each one
questions.prompt: In the MCP Apps extension, a tool's _meta.ui object carries resourceUri together with which other field?

Reject it, since client_id must exactly equal the URL the document was fetched from
questions.explanation: A Client ID Metadata Document is only valid when its client_id field is exactly equal to the URL it was fetched from, which anchors the identifier to a location the authorization server actually retrieved and validated. A mismatched client_id, even to a similar looking path on the same host, must be rejected rather than silently reconciled.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原D(3)CIMDclient_id fetchedURL exact，不同path即reject，TLS fetch安全/redirect登记当前policy仍核。
source_correct_options: Reject it, since client_id must exactly equal the URL the document was fetched from

questions.objective: Apply OAuth-based authorization, client registration, scopes, and user consent so a user approves what a server may see and do
questions.prompt: An authorization server advertises both client_id_metadata_document_supported and a registration_endpoint for Dynamic Client Registration, and the client has no pre-registered credentials for it. Which two statements about registration priority are correct? Select two.
options: Dynamic Client Registration should be attempted first since a registration_endpoint is present
Dynamic Client Registration remains usable as a fallback but is considered deprecated
Client ID Metadata Documents should be preferred here over Dynamic Client Registration
Asking the user to manually enter credentials is required before either mechanism is tried
questions.explanation: The registration priority places Client ID Metadata Documents ahead of Dynamic Client Registration whenever the authorization server advertises support for both, reserving DCR as a deprecated fallback rather than a first choice. Asking the user is the last resort, used only when neither automated mechanism nor pre-registration is available at all.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原B/C(1,2)本issuer未preconfig优先advertisedCIMD，DCRdeprecatedfallback；unsupported/invalidfetch不能无政策silentdowngrade。
source_correct_options: Dynamic Client Registration remains usable as a fallback but is considered deprecated
Client ID Metadata Documents should be preferred here over Dynamic Client Registration

questions.objective: Choose risk and safety controls against tool poisoning, injection, token misuse, and over-broad access
questions.prompt: A client receives a 403 response with error="insufficient_scope" and a scope value listing records:write. Which two actions describe a correct step-up authorization response? Select two.
options: Apply a limited number of retries rather than looping on repeated 403 responses indefinitely
Request the union of the previously granted scopes and the newly required scopes
Treat the 403 as a permanent denial and stop attempting the operation entirely
Discard any previously granted scopes and request only records:write going forward
questions.explanation: Stepping up authorization means asking for the union of whatever scopes were already granted plus the newly required ones, so existing access is not lost, while a bounded retry count prevents an endless challenge loop if the server keeps demanding more. Dropping prior scopes or treating the challenge as final both misread what a 403 response is asking for.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原A/B(0,1)有界stepupunion，需要用户/AS允许，用户拒/政策禁时可stop而非必须不断AS尝试；token字符串本地加scope无效。
source_correct_options: Apply a limited number of retries rather than looping on repeated 403 responses indefinitely
Request the union of the previously granted scopes and the newly required scopes

questions.objective: Choose risk and safety controls against tool poisoning, injection, token misuse, and over-broad access
questions.prompt: A server sends a form mode elicitation asking the user to confirm a destructive delete, and the ElicitResult that comes back is {"action":"decline"}. What must the server do?
options: Not perform the destructive action, since decline is an explicit refusal rather than an accept
Retry the same elicitation immediately using a new requestState until the user accepts
Treat decline the same as cancel and silently discard both the request and any response
Proceed with the delete anyway, since a decline still counts as an implicit confirmation
questions.explanation: ElicitResult defines accept, decline, and cancel as distinct outcomes, and decline specifically means the user explicitly refused, which is different from an ambiguous dismissal under cancel. A server that proceeded with the destructive action after a decline would be ignoring the one signal the elicitation was designed to capture.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原A(0)decline明确拒/不effect，cancel放弃不同事件，不骚扰自动retry；应正常响应business结果而非silentlydiscard。
source_correct_options: Not perform the destructive action, since decline is an explicit refusal rather than an accept

questions.objective: Choose risk and safety controls against tool poisoning, injection, token misuse, and over-broad access
questions.prompt: A server encodes requestState as plain base64 of {"user":"alice","op":"delete_account"}, with nothing else applied. What security property is this design missing?
options: A human readable format, since base64 makes the state impossible for anyone to decode
Integrity protection such as an HMAC or AEAD so the client cannot tamper with the state
A resultType field, since requestState is not permitted to appear without one
Compression, since the encoded state would otherwise be too large to fit in a retry
questions.explanation: Because requestState is attacker controlled input that a client can freely edit before echoing it back, plain base64 encoding provides no protection at all against tampering. When the state can influence authorization or business logic it needs integrity protection such as an HMAC or AEAD, bound to the principal, a short expiry, and the originating request.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原B(1)Base64无integrity，HMAC/AEAD必要时绑定可信principal/tenant/fullargs/policy/expiry/nonceatomicclaim；signed不替首次授权。
source_correct_options: Integrity protection such as an HMAC or AEAD so the client cannot tamper with the state

questions.objective: Choose risk and safety controls against tool poisoning, injection, token misuse, and over-broad access
questions.prompt: A tool's inputSchema contains a property defined as {"$ref": "https://schemas.example.net/address.json"}. What must a compliant implementation do before using this schema to validate arguments?
options: Reject the entire tool definition outright, since $ref is not part of JSON Schema 2020-12
Fetch the referenced schema automatically the first time the tool is called, caching it after
Not auto-dereference the network reference by default, allowing it only opt-in with an allowlist
Replace the $ref with an empty object schema and validate every argument as automatically valid
questions.explanation: Network references inside a JSON Schema are a denial of service and server side request forgery risk, so an implementation must not automatically dereference them, only doing so when explicitly opted in with a host allowlist, no private addresses, and timeouts. $ref itself is a normal 2020-12 keyword, so rejecting the whole schema outright is not correct either.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原C(2)不默认auto networkref，受控opt-in/allowlist/privateblock/time/budget；拒整tool可组织加严而非$ref非法，relative/$id/其它URI也需解析政策。
source_correct_options: Not auto-dereference the network reference by default, allowing it only opt-in with an allowlist

questions.objective: Choose risk and safety controls against tool poisoning, injection, token misuse, and over-broad access
questions.prompt: A tool's inputSchema marks a string property api_key and a string property region with x-mcp-header, so each value would be mirrored into an Mcp-Param header. Which two statements about this definition are correct? Select two.
options: Mirroring both is fine, since header values are encrypted separately from the JSON body
region must become a number, since only numeric values may be mirrored into headers
An HTTP client must drop a tool from tools/list if its x-mcp-header values are invalid
api_key should not be marked, since header values are visible to network intermediaries
questions.explanation: Header values are visible to intermediaries such as proxies, load balancers, and logging systems, so server developers should not mark sensitive parameters such as API keys with x-mcp-header; base64 encoding is not encryption. Mirroring is limited to integer, string, and boolean parameters, and a Streamable HTTP client must exclude a tool whose x-mcp-header values violate the constraints from its tools/list result.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原C/D(2,3)HTTP工具invalidx-mcp-header除目录/敏感apikey SHOULDNOT标，Base64非保密，TLSterminatingproxy仍可见；regionstring合法非仅number。
source_correct_options: An HTTP client must drop a tool from tools/list if its x-mcp-header values are invalid
api_key should not be marked, since header values are visible to network intermediaries

questions.objective: Design auditability and observability so protocol activity can be traced, attributed, and reviewed
questions.prompt: A request's _meta includes a key named traceparent holding a W3C Trace Context value, with no dot separated prefix before it. Why is this key name still valid under the _meta naming rules?
options: Because any key shorter than twelve characters is automatically exempt from the prefix requirement
Because traceparent was registered by the requesting client as its own custom capability
Because OpenTelemetry keys are only valid inside result._meta, never inside a request's _meta
Because traceparent, tracestate, and baggage are the one named exception to the prefix rule
questions.explanation: The _meta key naming rules generally require a dot separated prefix, but traceparent, tracestate, and baggage are called out as the one explicit exception so that standard W3C Trace Context and Baggage formats can be carried unmodified for OpenTelemetry propagation. No general exemption exists for short keys or client registered names.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原D(3)最接近但题/解释错：普通_meta prefix本来optional，sourcebrief§3也如此，不能说generallyrequireprefix；三个OTelbarekey是专门标准保留/允许形式，extensionprefix才mandatory。
source_correct_options: Because traceparent, tracestate, and baggage are the one named exception to the prefix rule

questions.objective: Design auditability and observability so protocol activity can be traced, attributed, and reviewed
questions.prompt: An audit pipeline receives a request whose _meta carries "traceparent":"00-00000000000000000000000000000000-00f067aa0ba902b7-01". What is wrong with this value?
options: An all-zero trace id is invalid, so the value cannot correlate spans across hops
The version field must be 01, since version 00 marks a trace that was sampled out
The flags field must be dropped whenever a trace crosses between two MCP servers
traceparent must sit under io.modelcontextprotocol/traceparent, not as a bare key
questions.explanation: A W3C traceparent is a version, a trace id, a parent id, and flags in lowercase hex, and an all-zero trace id is invalid by definition, so this value cannot tie the request to any trace. traceparent, tracestate, and baggage are the one named exception to the _meta prefix rule, so the bare key itself is correct.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原A(0)zeroTrace非法，core处理invalid可discard/restartcontext不必拒业务；version00非sampling，flagsbit1才sampled，zeroParent也invalid。
source_correct_options: An all-zero trace id is invalid, so the value cannot correlate spans across hops

questions.objective: Map the roles, responsibilities, governance, and adoption patterns of teams building and deploying MCP
questions.prompt: A publisher submits a server.json whose version field is "^1.4.0". What does the MCP Registry do with it, and who owns the fix?
options: Rejects it because the version must equal the protocol revision, such as 2026-07-28
Rejects it as a version range, so the publisher must publish one exact version
Accepts it, since server.json version strings are free text the registry never parses
Accepts it and resolves the range to the newest matching release at install time
questions.explanation: The registry prohibits version strings that look like ranges, such as ^1.4.0 or >=1.4.0, so the publisher, who owns the server.json, must publish one exact version per entry. The server.json version is the server's own release version and is unrelated to the protocol revision the server speaks.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原B(1)sourceRegistryexactversion非range，与schema/wireversion独立；真实已publishimmutable/artifactstatus/owner与现官方要核。
source_correct_options: Rejects it as a version range, so the publisher must publish one exact version

questions.objective: Map the roles, responsibilities, governance, and adoption patterns of teams building and deploying MCP
questions.prompt: A proposed spec change has reached Final status in the SEP process. What does that status require to have been satisfied?
options: A minimum of three unrelated SDK implementations shipping the change before it can be proposed
A rewrite of the entire specification document rather than a single dated revision
A completed reference implementation plus, for observable behavior, a conformance test
Unanimous approval from every registered MCP server operator in the public registry
questions.explanation: Under the SEP guidelines a proposal moves from accepted to Final only once its reference implementation is complete and, for a Standards Track change with observable protocol behavior, a conformance scenario has been merged. Implementation counts, operator votes, and whole document rewrites are not part of that bar.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原C(2)sourceSEP finalreferenceimplementation/observableconformancetest，行政workflow未本轮全页新核，StandardsTrack限定不能泛所有SEPtype。
source_correct_options: A completed reference implementation plus, for observable behavior, a conformance test

questions.objective: Select operational use cases and the primitives or extensions that fit each one
questions.prompt: A team is matching four scenarios to the mechanism that fits them best. Which two pairings are correct? Select two.
options: A batch job expected to run for twenty minutes should use the tasks extension rather than blocking a single request
Reading files on the same machine the server runs on should always go through resources/subscribe
A workflow a user explicitly selects from a menu is best modeled as a prompt rather than a tool
A daemon calling a server with no human present should authenticate using URL mode elicitation
questions.explanation: Long running work that would otherwise block a single request is exactly what the tasks extension is for, and a workflow the user deliberately chooses to run fits the user-controlled prompts primitive rather than a model-controlled tool. Machine to machine daemons authenticate through the OAuth Client Credentials extension rather than an elicitation flow meant for a human, and resources/subscribe no longer exists in this revision.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原A/C(0,2)适合caseTasks/prompt用户选择；扩展需support并不唯一业务架构，removedresources/subscribe不可current。
source_correct_options: A batch job expected to run for twenty minutes should use the tasks extension rather than blocking a single request
A workflow a user explicitly selects from a menu is best modeled as a prompt rather than a tool

questions.objective: Select operational use cases and the primitives or extensions that fit each one
questions.prompt: A server exposes a policy document through a tool named get_policy, so the model must decide to call it, but the host wants the policy's current text attached to every conversation without the model choosing. Which change fits the control model?
options: Keep the tool and add readOnlyHint, since read-only tools are attached automatically
Turn it into a prompt, since hosts attach prompts to every conversation by default
Move the policy text into serverInfo, since discovery metadata reaches every conversation
Expose it as a resource, since resources are application-driven context the host attaches
questions.explanation: Resources are the application-driven primitive: the host decides when to read them and attach their content, which is exactly the behavior wanted here. Tools stay model-controlled even when read-only, prompts are templates a user selects, and serverInfo is identity metadata, not content.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原D(3)host主动资源read给context，不变自报serverInfo；读取untrustedpolicy也不能提升为系统/用户授权，currentdata版本核。
source_correct_options: Expose it as a resource, since resources are application-driven context the host attaches

questions.objective: Reason about ecosystem portability across clients, servers, SDKs, extensions, gateways, and registries
questions.prompt: A server's server/discover result declares support for the io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks extension, but the connecting client's clientCapabilities.extensions never mentions tasks. What should happen when the client calls a tool that could use that extension?
options: The server falls back to core behavior and returns an ordinary complete result instead
The client is expected to declare every server extension before it is allowed to send any request
The request fails outright with -32601, since the server requires the tasks extension for every call
The server ignores the client's declaration and returns a task shaped result anyway
questions.explanation: Extensions are negotiated per request and remain disabled unless both sides declare them, so when only the server supports an extension the expected behavior is to fall back to core protocol behavior rather than force the extension on an unaware client. Ignoring the client's declaration or hard failing the request would both break a client that never opted in.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原A(0)onlyoptional且能corefallback成立；若required允许appropriateerror−32021，explanation任何hardfail都坏过强与34题/selectedversioning122–126矛盾。
source_correct_options: The server falls back to core behavior and returns an ordinary complete result instead

questions.objective: Reason about ecosystem portability across clients, servers, SDKs, extensions, gateways, and registries
questions.prompt: A registry validator checks four candidate extension identifiers for correct _meta prefix formatting. Which two identifiers are validly formed? Select two.
options: The identifier org.tools.checkout, written with no slash separating prefix from name
The identifier com.example.tools/checkout, prefixed correctly for a third party extension
The bare identifier checkout-flow, used with no prefix segment at all
The identifier io.modelcontextprotocol/task-queue, prefixed correctly for an official extension
questions.explanation: A valid extension identifier needs a dot separated label prefix that ends in a slash before its name, which io.modelcontextprotocol/task-queue and com.example.tools/checkout both provide. checkout-flow has no prefix at all, and org.tools.checkout has dotted labels but never supplies the slash that would separate a prefix from a name.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原B/D(1,3)只是语法，officialreservedprefix不能第三方占；不是D例task-queue已官方implemented，名字不证capability。
source_correct_options: The identifier com.example.tools/checkout, prefixed correctly for a third party extension
The identifier io.modelcontextprotocol/task-queue, prefixed correctly for an official extension

questions.objective: Select operational use cases and the primitives or extensions that fit each one
questions.prompt: A resources/read for ui://reports/summary returns {"contents":[{"uri":"ui://reports/summary","mimeType":"text/html","text":"<!DOCTYPE html>..."}]}. Why will an MCP Apps host not render this resource as an app?
options: The HTML must arrive in a blob field, since hosts refuse to render text content
The mimeType must be text/html;profile=mcp-app for a host to treat it as an app
The contents entry must carry a visibility array naming who may open the app
The uri must use https:// instead of ui://, since hosts only fetch apps over HTTPS
questions.explanation: A UI resource is recognized by its mime type: the resources/read contents entry must be text/html;profile=mcp-app, and plain text/html is just an ordinary resource. ui:// is the required scheme for UI resources, the HTML may arrive as text or as a blob, and visibility belongs on the tool's _meta.ui, not on the resource.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原B(1)fixedAppsMIMEprofile，HTML可text/blob；片段contentsresult还须resultType/cachefields，UI资源scheme/完整HTML/hostpolicy核。
source_correct_options: The mimeType must be text/html;profile=mcp-app for a host to treat it as an app

questions.objective: Reason about ecosystem portability across clients, servers, SDKs, extensions, gateways, and registries
questions.prompt: A resources/read result for a ui:// resource carries this contents entry _meta on one line: {"ui": {"csp": ["https://cdn.example.com", "https://api.example.com"]}}. What is wrong with how csp is expressed here?
options: mimeType is missing from this contents entry, which is the only actual problem here
csp belongs on the tool's _meta.ui rather than on the resource's _meta.ui at all
csp must be an object with keys like connectDomains and frameDomains, not a flat array of origins
The two origins listed must instead be combined into a single comma separated string
questions.explanation: The csp field on a UI resource's _meta.ui is an object whose optional keys such as connectDomains, resourceDomains, frameDomains, and baseUriDomains each hold a list of origins for a specific content security policy directive, not a single flat array of origins. A flat list like this does not tell the host which directive each origin applies to.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原C(2)CSPobject四名单分directive，错array拒/安全fallback；permissionsemptyobject不同，域合法/currentpolicy/actualbrowser独立。
source_correct_options: csp must be an object with keys like connectDomains and frameDomains, not a flat array of origins

questions.objective: Reason about ecosystem portability across clients, servers, SDKs, extensions, gateways, and registries
questions.prompt: A registry entry's server.json declares its name as io.github.acme-labs/weather-tools. What does this namespace form require the registry to have verified before accepting the entry?
options: That the server only exposes tools and never exposes any resources or prompts
That the server passed every SDK Tier 1 conformance test before publication
That the package has been downloaded at least once from npm, PyPI, or Docker
That acme-labs actually controls the io.github.acme-labs namespace, through a GitHub, DNS, or HTTP challenge
questions.explanation: The registry uses reverse DNS namespaces so that a name like io.github.acme-labs carries an ownership claim, and admission requires proving control of that namespace through a GitHub, DNS, or HTTP challenge rather than trusting the string on its face. Conformance tier, download counts, and which primitives a server exposes are unrelated to namespace verification.

source_correct_options: That acme-labs actually controls the io.github.acme-labs namespace, through a GitHub, DNS, or HTTP challenge

questions.objective: Map the roles, responsibilities, governance, and adoption patterns of teams building and deploying MCP
questions.prompt: An SDK maintainer claims their SDK meets the bar for Tier 1 under the SDK tiering system. Which combination of facts would actually support that claim?
options: It passes 100 percent of conformance tests and fixes critical bugs within seven days
It passes 100 percent of conformance tests but takes a month to triage newly reported issues
It is labeled experimental and has no committed timeline for triaging reported issues
It passes 80 percent of conformance tests and ships new features within six months of a spec release
questions.explanation: Tier 1 requires passing all conformance tests, shipping features ahead of a spec release, triaging issues within two business days, and fixing critical bugs within seven days. Passing only 80 percent or taking a month to triage describes a lower tier or a slipping Tier 1 SDK, not one that actually meets the Tier 1 bar.

questions.objective: Reason about ecosystem portability across clients, servers, SDKs, extensions, gateways, and registries
questions.prompt: A transcript otherwise built entirely from 2026-07-28 style requests includes one early message: {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2026-07-28"}}. What is wrong with including this message in a modern flow?
options: The protocolVersion value inside params is written in the wrong date format for this revision
The initialize method was removed in this revision, since version and capability data now travel per request
initialize is fine here as long as no notifications/initialized message ever follows it
initialize is still required, but only as the very first message on a Streamable HTTP connection
questions.explanation: The 2026-07-28 revision removed the initialize handshake and the paired notifications/initialized entirely, replacing them with per-request _meta fields such as protocolVersion and clientCapabilities on every message. Even a correctly formatted protocolVersion value does not rescue a method that no longer exists in this revision, on stdio or on Streamable HTTP.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原B(1)currentcore没有initialize，Apps uiinitialize独立UIversion存在；不能替换名字/传2026-07-28救旧core。
source_correct_options: The initialize method was removed in this revision, since version and capability data now travel per request

questions.objective: Select operational use cases and the primitives or extensions that fit each one
questions.prompt: A client declares the tasks extension, and a server that supports it still answers a quick lookup tool call with an ordinary CallToolResult carrying resultType complete instead of a CreateTaskResult. What does this demonstrate about choosing among the available interaction patterns?
options: The client must redeclare the tasks extension on every request or the server ignores it silently
The server made a specification error, since declaring the tasks extension forces every result to be a task
The server decides per request whether a task is warranted, and a quick call does not need one
A complete result and a task result are simply interchangeable labels for the same behavior
questions.explanation: Declaring an extension only makes it available for a given request, it does not obligate the server to use it every time, and the tasks extension itself lets the server decide per request whether the work actually needs a task handle versus finishing inline. Reserving tasks for work that genuinely runs long avoids the polling overhead a task would add to an already fast call.

metadata.title: MCPA Full-Length Mock 3: Design and Security Trade-offs

questions.objective: Describe the core MCP concepts of hosts, clients, servers, primitives, and the stateless JSON-RPC request model
questions.prompt: A team migrating to MCP 2026-07-28 complains that servers can no longer remember a shopping cart between calls the way a session used to. What does the stateless design actually require them to do instead, and why is that the right trade?
options: Mint a server handle for the cart, return it in a result, and have the client pass it back as an argument
Open one dedicated connection to a single replica so that replica can hold the cart in its own memory
Send an initialize request each morning so the server can attach the cart to that entire day's ongoing handshake process every time
Resend the entire cart's contents inside the JSON-RPC id field on every single request the client makes
questions.explanation: Statelessness means a server cannot rely on a prior request on the same connection, so any state that must span calls needs an explicit, server-minted, opaque handle passed back as a normal argument. That is what lets any replica answer any request, which is the whole payoff of dropping sessions.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原A(0)explicitopaquehandle不权限capability，store跨replica/currentACL/生命周期/atomic重要，否则任意replica仍错。
source_correct_options: Mint a server handle for the cart, return it in a result, and have the client pass it back as an argument

questions.objective: Describe the core MCP concepts of hosts, clients, servers, primitives, and the stateless JSON-RPC request model
questions.prompt: A backend engineer proposes storing per-client state keyed by the underlying TCP connection so a server can skip re-reading arguments on every call. Why does this design break the 2026-07-28 statelessness guarantee even if it works in a single-server test?
options: It requires every client to install a new certificate before it can open any connection at all
It makes a call's outcome depend on which connection carried it, so no other replica can serve it correctly
It duplicates work that tools/list pagination already performs whenever a result set grows large across many separate paginated requests
It is disallowed only because TCP connections run slower than the stdio transport for local servers
questions.explanation: Connection-keyed state reintroduces exactly the stickiness that 2026-07-28 removed: a load balancer could route the next call to a different replica, or the client could reconnect, and the server would answer incorrectly. The fix is an explicit handle carried in the request, not implicit connection memory.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原B(1)TCPsession依赖破逐请求上下文，明示handle允许业务state，不要求server任何memory都无。
source_correct_options: It makes a call's outcome depend on which connection carried it, so no other replica can serve it correctly

questions.objective: Read the MCP specification, its revision history, and its feature lifecycle to tell current, deprecated, and removed behavior apart
questions.prompt: A team debating how to pin its integration asks why MCP names revisions with dates such as 2026-07-28 instead of semantic version numbers. What does the date in a revision identifier signify?
options: The day every earlier revision stopped working, since each date retires older revisions
The day the revision's governance vote closed, whatever the revision happened to change
The last date backwards incompatible changes were made, so compatible updates keep it
The release date of the newest SDK that implements the revision's full feature set
questions.explanation: A protocol version string is a date in YYYY-MM-DD form marking the last date backwards incompatible changes were made; the specification can still receive backwards compatible updates without changing it. Older revisions do not stop working on that date, and SDK release dates or governance votes play no part in the identifier.
questions.chinese_judgment: 原C(2)revisiondate代表lastbackwardsbreaking，fixedversion+commit防同日兼容drift，oldrevision不自动失效。
source_correct_options: The last date backwards incompatible changes were made, so compatible updates keep it

questions.objective: Reason about interoperability, protocol versioning, and the value of one open protocol over per-system custom integrations
questions.prompt: A company already has a proprietary message format tuned exactly to its internal tools and refuses to adopt MCP, arguing their format is simpler for their own use. What is the clearest cost of that choice as new AI hosts and external systems appear?
options: Their format will automatically gain OAuth 2.1 support the moment a new host adopts it
Nothing changes at all, since message formats never affect how many separate integrations a team must eventually build

questions.prompt: A client was built and tested only against one specific MCP server. Under 2026-07-28, why should that same client generally be able to work against a different, unrelated, modern server without code changes?

Yes, since any function at all becomes more valuable once it is exposed through a protocol
